extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, patent practitioners, USPTO staff, and researchers studying patent examination outcomes and Section 101 case law effects
extracted.subtask_description: Quantitative analysis of USPTO first-office-action outcomes and examiner-level variability (uncertainty) in patent subject-matter eligibility decisions following Alice and subsequent USPTO guidance. The report defines metrics, samples, and identification of affected technologies to measure changes over time and across examiner cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of first office action Section 101 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric used to capture the relative change in first office actions that include rejections for patent-ineligible subject matter (Section 101). It increases when examiners issue relatively more first office actions with a Section 101 rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed by dividing the total number of first office action decisions containing a Section 101 rejection by the total number of first office actions and multiplying by 100 for each time period by technology category. The data capture all types of Section 101 rejections, including utility and statutory double patenting. Note: this metric focuses on first office actions and does not capture the full breadth of patent examination activities leading to a first office action. Sample restrictions apply (see sample restriction metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 101 first action examination uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric that captures the variation across examiners in the proportion of first-office-action rejections for patent-ineligible subject matter; uncertainty increases when the percentage of first-office-action Section 101 rejections becomes more uneven across examiners within a technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculated by (1) for each examiner within a USPC technology and a specified time period, computing the examiner's rate = (# first office actions containing a Section 101 rejection) / (total # first office actions by that examiner in that USPC and time period); (2) computing the variance across those examiner rates in each USPC for a half-year time period; and (3) averaging the variance across USPCs within the Alice-affected technology set (and likewise for the control set). Time intervals used are half-year periods (e.g., Jan–Jun; Jul–Dec for Alice; other intervals for Berkheimer/2019 PEG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Alice-affected technologies (USPC mapping via OPLA litigation records)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of technologies considered 'Alice-affected' is formed from United States Patent Classifications (USPCs) of patent applications that were litigated for 'abstract ideas' according to the USPTO Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OPLA's documentation of patents-in-suit and the relevant judicial exception for each case to identify the USPCs involved in Section 101 litigation. The control set ('other technologies') includes all USPCs that were never involved in patent litigation for Section 101 issues per OPLA records. Note: USPC schema is now dormant and no longer reported by the USPTO; supplementary data cited (ieg-sme_crt_dec.xlsx) were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample restriction: include only applications filed before the event date
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize influence from applicant drafting, filing decisions, or other applicant behavior changes in response to judicial or USPTO guidance, the analysis considers only patent applications filed before the relevant event (Alice decision or 2019 PEG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Alice effects, include only applications filed before June 19, 2014. For evaluating the 2019 PEG, include only applications filed before January 7, 2019. Because the composition of applications differs at each event date, samples used to study different events are not directly comparable (e.g., Figure 1 sample differs from Figure 3 sample).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the first office action (first decision by examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: The analysis concentrates on the examiner's first decision on patentability (the first office action) to reduce complexity in separating examiner behavior from applicant behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: focusing on first office actions reduces confounding from later prosecution events and applicant responses. MPEP references (see MPEP §§706–707) are used to define first office action stages. The chosen metrics are computed at the first action stage only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Section 101 rejections and scope under Alice
rubrics_metrics.description: Alice held that generic computer implementation does not transform a patent-ineligible abstract idea into a patent-eligible invention and effectively broadened the scope of ineligible subject matter; ambiguity in Alice's language created interpretive latitude across practitioners and examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report treats Alice as an event that could expand Section 101 rejections across technologies and increase uncertainty due to differing reasonable interpretations. Empirically, the report measures how the probability of first-office-action Section 101 rejections and examination uncertainty changed following Alice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Berkheimer memorandum requirement for factual findings on conventionality
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO April 2018 Berkheimer memorandum changed examiner instructions by requiring examiners to make a factual determination as to whether claim elements were common, well-understood, routine, or conventional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to the memorandum, examiners were not required to support such conclusions with factual evidence. The memorandum's requirement to record factual determinations is treated as a policy change that can affect the rate of Section 101 rejections and inter-examiner variability; the report measures its empirical impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2019 PEG grouping of abstract ideas and 'practical application' guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's January 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG) clarified legal distinctions: abstract ideas are grouped as mathematical concepts, certain methods of organizing human activity, and mental processes; a claim that recites an abstract idea is not 'directed to' the abstract idea if the claim as a whole integrates the abstract idea into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2019 PEG is treated as a structured clarification intended to reduce interpretive latitude and improve consistency. The report measures the PEG's effect on reducing first-office-action Section 101 rejections and examiner-level uncertainty (finding substantial decreases after its issuance). The report also points readers to USPTO training and materials on implementing the 2019 PEG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for other rejection types and comparative inference
rubrics_metrics.description: In assessing the effect of Alice and USPTO guidance, the analysis uses other technologies (USPCs without Section 101 litigation) as a control group and examines other first-office-action rejection types (Sections 102, 103, 112) for changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The control group captures influence of unrelated events. The report notes that other rejection types (102, 103, 112) do not show statistically significant changes after Alice, supporting inference that observed changes are specific to Section 101 developments. See supplementary materials for statistical details.
